categoryName: Laundry — detergent powder & liquid, bars, softener, bleach, stain remover, hangers, pegs, iron aids

skuLines.examples: Ghadi, Nirma, Wheel Active, Fena
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; volume spike at term start (Apr, Jul) when hostels refill
skuLines.notes: The single largest volume line in the category. MRP-printed and price-shopped, so margin is thin — earn on it with the 4kg pack, not the 500g. Powder cakes and lumps in Baru Sahib's monsoon humidity: store on pallets off the floor, prefer poly pouches over cartons, hold no more than 8-10 weeks of cover.

skuLines.examples: Rin Advanced, Tide Plus Jasmine & Rose, Wheel Complete, Fena Ultra
skuLines.notes: The staff-quarters default: a step up from Ghadi/Nirma without paying Surf money. Same humidity-caking caution as economy powder.

skuLines.examples: Surf Excel Easy Wash, Ariel Complete, Tide Ultra
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; lifts before Gurpurab, Baisakhi and convocation/function weeks when whites must look new
skuLines.notes: Carry one premium powder, not three. In a captive market the premium buyer is a defined, countable set of staff households — stock to that number rather than to a shelf-share instinct.

skuLines.examples: Surf Excel Matic Top Load, Surf Excel Matic Front Load, Ariel Matic, Tide Matic
skuLines.notes: Married-staff quarters run semi-automatic and automatic machines; a non-matic powder foams over and they blame the store. Stock top-load and front-load as SEPARATE lines — they are not interchangeable and front-load is the smaller, higher-value tail. Low-foam matic powder is also what the campus laundry/mess machines need.

skuLines.examples: Ghadi 5kg/10kg, Nirma bulk, Fena bulk, local Punjab/HP bulk-fill powder
skuLines.seasonality: Monthly institutional indent; pre-monsoon (May-Jun) stock-up against hill-road closures
skuLines.notes: Not a consumer line — this is the hostel laundry, mess, canteen and guest-house indent, and it is the most freight-efficient rupee in the category (₹/kg of freight is lowest on a sack). Sell on a monthly indent against an institutional account, not off the shelf. Best single lever for turning laundry from thin-margin retail into contracted volume.

skuLines.examples: Ghadi ₹1/₹2, Nirma ₹1, Wheel ₹2, Rin ₹5
skuLines.packSizes: ₹1 / ₹2 / ₹5 / ₹10 sachet, sold loose or in a 16-32 sachet strip
skuLines.notes: This is how a 5-18-year-old with pocket money and no cupboard space actually buys detergent. Never stock out — a sachet stock-out is the moment a student's wallet starts leaking to a town trip. Zero freight drag, sells by the strip at the counter, ideal for Ary Lite.

skuLines.examples: Rin Colour Care, Surf Excel Colour Care, Ariel colour-safe
skuLines.notes: Real need here: coloured dastaars, dupattas and salwar-kameez bleed badly in ordinary powder plus blue. One SKU is enough; the same job is often done better by the delicates liquid line.

skuLines.examples: Ghadi bar, Nirma bar, Wheel bar, Fena bar, 555, Xpert
skuLines.notes: Hand-washing dominates a hostel and a cold-water hill bathroom, so the bar is a co-equal workhorse with powder, not a legacy format. Bars travel and store better than anything else in the lane: no leakage, no caking, lowest freight per rupee. Sikh institution — carry bars whose wrapper declares plant/vegetable-derived fatty acid where the option exists, because tallow-based soap will be asked about.

skuLines.examples: Rin Advanced bar, Surf Excel bar, Tide bar
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks with sports/PT season and monsoon mud
skuLines.notes: The collar-and-cuff bar. School whites plus playground mud is the exact job this format wins.

skuLines.examples: Dettol bar for laundry use, neem washing bar, carbolic (red) soap
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon (Jul-Sep) and any infection scare in a hostel block
skuLines.notes: In a residential school a single skin infection or a lice round makes this line sell out in days. Shared bathrooms plus damp mean hygiene-positioned laundry soap has a permanent, not fad, place here.

skuLines.examples: Surf Excel Matic Liquid (Top Load / Front Load), Ariel Matic Liquid, Tide Liquid
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; lifts in winter when cold water dissolves powder poorly
skuLines.notes: Liquid is the fastest-growing format in Indian laundry and the one a captive store most often under-stocks. Hill logistics work against it: heavy, low value per kg, and bottles crush and leak on 30-50km of hill road — insist on shrink-wrapped shippers and buy the refill pouch alongside. Liquids also thicken and can cloud below ~5°C, so don't store them in an unheated winter godown.

skuLines.examples: Surf Excel hand-wash liquid, Rin liquid, Nirma liquid, Fena liquid
skuLines.notes: Dissolves in cold hill water where powder leaves residue and white marks on dark clothes — the single most common complaint hand-washers have, and the reason this line converts.

skuLines.examples: Godrej Ezee, Genteel, Comfort delicate wash, Safewash
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp season: Oct-Mar, strongest Nov-Feb. Sirmaur hill winters put every resident into sweaters, shawls and thermals
skuLines.notes: The most under-appreciated must-have in this lane for THIS location. Ordinary detergent felts and shrinks wool, and a ruined sweater in a cold township is a real loss. Buy the winter's whole requirement in one pre-season consignment (Sep) — it is a seasonal line, so a mid-winter stock-out cannot be recovered. Also the correct product for shawls and fine dupattas.

skuLines.examples: Mamaearth Plant-Based Baby Laundry Liquid, Himalaya baby laundry wash, Pigeon Liquid Laundry Detergent, Mee Mee, Bumtum
skuLines.notes: Married staff with small children and babies is an explicitly named cohort here, and this is the line they will drive to town for if it is missing. High margin, low weight, long shelf life — one of the few genuinely profitable laundry lines. Keep it near baby care, not buried in detergents. Also the right product for cloth-nappy households.

skuLines.examples: Beco, Koparo Clean, The Better Home, Bhuumi, Nimyle laundry
skuLines.notes: Best margin in the lane, thinnest demand. Justified here by two things beyond fashion: concentrates cut freight per wash on a hill road, and greywater from 5,000 people goes into a hill catchment, so a low-phosphate claim has an institutional buyer, not just a retail one. Start with one facing; do not build a shelf.

skuLines.examples: Surf Excel Matic refill pouch, Ariel Matic refill, Ezee refill, Comfort refill
skuLines.notes: The right answer to this store's core constraint. A pouch ships at a fraction of a bottle's cube and weight, does not crack, and is cheaper per wash — so it wins on hill freight, on shelf space and on the resident's wallet at once. Push it deliberately: sell the bottle once, the pouch forever.

skuLines.examples: Ariel pods, Wype laundry sheets, Zerocircle / eco laundry strips
skuLines.notes: 2026's format story and almost weightless — a sheet pack is the cheapest thing in this lane to freight up a hill, which is exactly the arbitrage a remote store should test. Real caution: pods are a poisoning risk with small children and babies on campus, so if stocked they must be sold in child-resistant tubs and never loose. Test 2 SKUs, one facing.

skuLines.examples: Ujala Supreme, Robin Liquid Blue, Rangeela
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; sharp peaks before Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Nagar Kirtan, sports day, convocation and exam weeks
skuLines.notes: For a Sikh institution this is a hero line, not an adjunct. White dastaars, patkas, kurtas, school whites and chef whites all go grey without it, and four drops cost a rupee — so it is bought constantly by nearly everyone. If one whitener SKU can never be out of stock, it is this one. Tiny, unbreakable, near-zero freight.

skuLines.examples: Robin Blue Powder pouch, Robin tikki, loose neel
skuLines.notes: The older format the liquid replaced in cities but not in hill and small-town India — elderly residents and the campus dhobi/laundry still ask for tikki by name, and it is the cheapest whitening per wash for a bucket of institutional whites. Stocking it is a cohort decision, not a nostalgia one.

skuLines.line: Whitening detergent additive / instant whitener powder
skuLines.examples: Ujala IDD, Mr. White, Safed, Ala
skuLines.notes: A booster added to ordinary powder to rescue yellowed whites, which is exactly what iron-bearing hill borewell water causes. Cheaper for the resident than trading up to a premium detergent, and better margin for the store — a genuinely aligned trade-up.

skuLines.examples: Vanish Oxi Action powder, Vanish Oxi Action liquid, Ariel Oxy booster
skuLines.notes: Safe on colours where chlorine bleach is not, which makes it the only bleach most families should be sold. Hygroscopic — it loses activity if it sits damp, so keep it sealed and off the floor in monsoon and do not carry deep cover.

skuLines.examples: Generic 4-5% sodium hypochlorite laundry bleach, Bleach liquid 5L institutional can
skuLines.notes: An institutional line for canteen linen, mess cloths, chef whites and hostel bedding — not something to push to families, who will ruin coloured clothes with it. Constraints are real: hypochlorite loses strength in roughly 6-12 months so it must not be deep-stocked, it corrodes and must never co-load or co-store with food or with acids/ammonia, and 5L cans want a bunded shelf. Sell it against the canteen and hostel accounts.

skuLines.line: Washing soda / soda ash & borax (pre-soak, hard-water aid)
skuLines.examples: Loose washing soda (soda ash), Sodium bicarbonate, Borax powder, water-softening salt
skuLines.notes: Hard, iron-bearing hill water is the invisible cause of grey whites, stiff cloth and scaled machines here, and washing soda is the ₹40 fix that also cuts how much detergent a wash needs. Loose-weight sale, excellent margin, indefinite shelf life, trivial freight. An underrated line for this exact location.

skuLines.line: All-purpose stain remover liquid / gel / spray
skuLines.examples: Vanish Oxi Action Gel, Vanish stain pen, Ariel stain remover, Sasmar spot remover
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; monsoon mud and function-wear rescue
skuLines.notes: Impulse-priced, high margin, light. Merchandise it beside the premium powder rather than in a chemicals aisle.

skuLines.examples: Ink stain remover liquid, Vanish pre-treat, isopropyl-based spot remover
skuLines.notes: Specific to a residential school: several thousand children using fountain and gel pens on white uniform shirts, every single week. This is a demand shape that a normal general store would not have and that a campus store must — an obvious win the ideal list should not miss.

skuLines.examples: Vanish Oxi for grease, degreaser spot spray, dishwash-based pre-treat
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; langar and canteen duty rosters, festival cooking
skuLines.notes: Turmeric and cooking-oil marks are the dominant stain in an Indian kitchen and in langar seva, and they defeat ordinary detergent. Canteen and mess staff are the repeat buyer.

skuLines.examples: Soak-and-wash enzyme powder, Vanish pre-soak, Surf Excel pre-soak use
skuLines.notes: Cold hill water badly weakens enzyme action, so soaking is what actually cleans here. A low-cost line that supports the hand-wash reality of this campus. Keep dry.

skuLines.examples: Comfort After Wash (Lily Fresh / Morning Fresh / Pure), Comfort Core, Downy
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks monsoon (Jul-Sep) and winter (Dec-Feb) when clothes dry indoors and go stiff and musty
skuLines.notes: In a heavy-monsoon cold hill township this stops being a luxury: it is what makes indoor-dried, hard-water-washed cloth soft and non-smelly. Heavy and leak-prone on hill transport — buy the large pack for staff quarters and lean on sachets for everyone else.

skuLines.examples: Comfort ₹1 / ₹2 / ₹5 sachet, Comfort 20ml pouch
skuLines.notes: How fabric conditioner is actually penetrating small-town and institutional India — sachet-first. It is also the only format a hostel student with no cupboard will buy. Sell off a counter strip; freight is negligible.

skuLines.line: Anti-bacterial / anti-damp laundry additive & laundry sanitiser
skuLines.examples: Comfort Anti-Bacterial, Dettol Antiseptic Liquid (laundry use), Savlon laundry, Comfort odour-shield
skuLines.seasonality: Hero line Jul-Sep monsoon; second peak Dec-Feb
skuLines.notes: The most location-specific must-have in the lane. Baru Sahib's monsoon means clothes cannot be sun-dried for weeks, and indoor-dried cloth in a cold hill room goes mildewed and sour — this is the product that fixes it, and residents will pay for it. Buy the monsoon requirement before the road gets unreliable in Jun.

skuLines.examples: Comfort fabric spray, Ambi Pur fabric, generic linen mist
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon; winter when clothes are re-worn rather than washed
skuLines.notes: Refreshes a blazer or a sweater that cannot be washed in a hill winter — a real between-washes job here. If pressurised, it is a flammable aerosol: transport and store away from heat, and keep it off a sunlit shelf.

skuLines.examples: Wrinkle-release spray, anti-crease mist
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; exam, interview and function days
skuLines.notes: A one-facing trial line. Its real buyer is a student or young staff member with no iron and a presentation in the morning.

skuLines.examples: Revive Instant Starch, generic instant starch powder
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; sharp peaks before Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Nagar Kirtan, sports day and convocation
skuLines.notes: Second hero line for a Sikh institution, alongside blue whitener. A dastaar and a patka must be starched to tie and hold at all, and school uniforms, kurtas and dupattas are starched routinely — so this sells to nearly every household every week. Light, dry, long shelf life, cheap to freight. Never let it go out of stock in a festival week.

skuLines.examples: Spray starch aerosol, Revive spray, instant collar-and-cuff starch
skuLines.notes: Convenience version of the powder for collars, cuffs and a single shirt. Pressurised aerosol: flammable-goods handling on the hill leg, no heat, no sun, and keep it out of the same shipper as food.

skuLines.line: Traditional loose starch / kanji (maida, arrowroot, sago)
skuLines.examples: Loose maida-kanji starch, arrowroot powder, sago/sabudana starch, rice starch
skuLines.notes: How dastaars and cotton suits are actually starched by many households and by the campus dhobi — boiled kanji, not a branded pack. Cheapest starch per garment by a wide margin, sold loose by weight at good margin. A branded-only assortment would miss this entirely, which is precisely the kind of gap a hill-store list must catch.

skuLines.examples: Iron plate cleaner stick, sole-plate cleaning paste, non-stick iron cleaner
skuLines.notes: Starch plus a hot iron burns onto the plate and then ruins the next white shirt — a direct consequence of how heavily this population starches. Sells as an attach to the starch line, which is where it should be merchandised.

skuLines.examples: Distilled water 1L / 5L can, scented ironing water
skuLines.notes: Hill borewell water scales and blocks a steam iron within months and then spits brown water on whites. Heavy for its value, so buy the 5L and, better, decant — or pair it with the washing-soda/descaling story rather than freighting water up a mountain.

skuLines.line: Ironing board, board cover & pressing accessories
skuLines.examples: Foldable ironing board, table-top ironing board, replacement board cover, pressing cloth, sleeve board, iron rest pad
skuLines.seasonality: Term start (Apr, Jul) and new-staff arrival months
skuLines.notes: Bulky and low value-density, so it is the worst freight in the lane per rupee — order boards once or twice a year in a single consignment with the drying racks, and keep the fast-moving replacement COVERS in continuous stock instead. A board outlives a cover by years, so covers are the repeat sale.

skuLines.examples: Generic plastic hangers, Kuber Industries, Amazon Basics, Cello
skuLines.seasonality: Hard spike at term start (Apr and Jul admissions) and hostel move-in; again at end of term
skuLines.notes: Best margin-to-effort line in the whole category and a certainty in a residential campus — every arriving student needs a dozen, every quarter needs more. Kids sizes matter: a 5-10-year-old's shirt falls off an adult hanger. Nests and stacks, so freight per unit is low. Stock deep before April and July, not after.

skuLines.examples: Wooden hangers, velvet flocked slim hangers, padded satin hangers
skuLines.seasonality: Winter (coats, blazers, shawls); wedding and function season
skuLines.notes: The natural attach at the clothing store — sold with the garment, not in the laundry aisle. Velvet slim hangers hold a dupatta or a shawl that slides off plastic, and wooden hangers are what a blazer or a woollen coat needs in a damp climate. Wooden hangers can mildew in monsoon storage; keep them dry.

skuLines.examples: Trouser/skirt clip hangers, 5-tier trouser hanger, multi-layer saree/dupatta hanger, cascading hooks
skuLines.notes: A hostel cupboard is small and shared, so anything that multiplies hanging space sells itself. Multi-tier dupatta and saree hangers have a specific buyer among staff women and university students here.

skuLines.examples: Plastic clothes pegs, stainless steel clips, wooden pegs, heavy-duty grip clips
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; replacement spike after monsoon and after windy spells
skuLines.notes: Consumable, not durable — cheap plastic pegs go brittle in UV and cold and snap in a season, which is the repeat sale. Stock STEEL pegs too: they are what actually survives a hill winter and monsoon, and what a 5-6m dastaar being stretched on a line needs to hold. Tiny, high-margin, near-zero freight.

skuLines.examples: Nylon washing line, PVC-coated steel wire line, braided cotton line, retractable line with hooks
skuLines.notes: Sell it loose by the metre as well as coiled — that is how a hostel warden or a quarters household actually buys it. Carry an EXTRA-LONG option deliberately: a dastaar is 5-6 metres of voile and needs a full run of line to stretch and dry, which a standard 10m domestic line cannot give alongside the rest of a family's wash. PVC-coated steel is the honest recommendation in a wet climate; nylon sags and stains whites with rust marks from any exposed wire.

skuLines.line: Foldable indoor / outdoor cloth drying stand
skuLines.examples: 2-tier and 3-tier steel drying stand, Bathla Mobidry, Peng Essentials, Magna
skuLines.seasonality: Hard peak pre-monsoon (May-Jun) and again in winter
skuLines.notes: In a heavy-monsoon cold hill township this is the highest-value durable in the lane: for weeks at a stretch there is no sun, and a family with a baby simply cannot function without indoor drying. Bulky and low value-density — bring the year's stock up in one pre-monsoon consignment with the ironing boards, and expect it to be a May-June and October event rather than a shelf line. Rust is the failure mode; buy powder-coated or stainless, not painted mild steel.

skuLines.line: Wall-mount, balcony & retractable ceiling drying rack
skuLines.examples: Ceiling-mounted pulley drying hanger, wall-folding balcony rack, retractable wall line
skuLines.notes: The permanent version for staff quarters, and the one that needs an installation service attached — which is a margin opportunity, not a friction. Fits where a floor stand does not, and keeps a small quarters room usable through the monsoon.

skuLines.examples: 16-clip octopus hanger, 8-peg round dryer, sock-and-innerwear hanging dryer
skuLines.notes: Perfect for what a hostel actually washes daily — socks, innerwear, handkerchiefs, patkas — in a space no bigger than a hook. Cheap, light, collapses flat for freight, and an easy impulse buy at the counter. Also what a baby's household needs for a dozen small items a day.

skuLines.examples: 15-20L bucket, 25-40L washing tub, tub with wringer, Cello / Nayasa / Milton
skuLines.notes: Hand-washing is the default here, so the bucket is laundry EQUIPMENT, not homeware — stock it in this lane. A wringer matters more than it looks: in a monsoon hill climate, how much water you get out by hand decides whether the clothes dry at all. Nests for freight if bought in matched sizes. Guaranteed April/July volume from hostel intake.

skuLines.line: Laundry basket, hamper & collapsible laundry bag
skuLines.examples: Plastic laundry basket, collapsible mesh hamper, cane/woven hamper, drawstring laundry bag
skuLines.notes: Every hostel bed and every quarters bathroom needs one. Collapsible bags are the freight-friendly version and the one a student travelling by bus can carry — stock those deep and the rigid baskets shallow, because rigid baskets ship air up a hill road.

skuLines.line: Mesh wash bags & delicates / lingerie nets
skuLines.examples: Zippered mesh laundry bags, lingerie wash net, sock wash bag, sweater net
skuLines.notes: Two real jobs on this campus: protecting delicates and woollens in a machine, and keeping one person's socks and innerwear identifiable in a shared hostel or communal laundry — which is a dignity and privacy point for women residents, not just convenience. Weightless, high margin.

skuLines.examples: Cloth washing brush, wooden/plastic washboard, collar-and-cuff scrub brush
skuLines.notes: The tool half of hand-washing, and still how collars, cuffs and muddy PT clothes get clean in cold water. Cheap, sells alongside the bar, and a normal urban assortment would drop it — here it belongs.

skuLines.line: Portable mini washing machine / bucket agitator
skuLines.examples: Mini portable washing machine (2.5-4 kg), bucket-mounted agitator, foot-pedal washer
skuLines.seasonality: Term start; winter (cold water makes hand-washing miserable)
skuLines.notes: A genuine emerging line for hostel and single-staff rooms where a full machine is impossible. Test 2-3 units before committing: it is a high-ticket, service-liability item on a hill with no repair shop nearby, so only stock it if a repair path exists.

skuLines.examples: Lint roller with refill sheets, electric fabric shaver, lint comb, sticky roller
skuLines.seasonality: Winter (Oct-Mar) — the whole season is woollens
skuLines.notes: Six months of sweaters, shawls and blankets in a hill winter means pilling and lint on everything, especially on dark clothes and on a dastaar. The REFILL is the repeat sale — stock refills deeper than rollers. Light, high margin, strongly seasonal: land it in September.

skuLines.line: Laundry name marker pen & printed name tapes
skuLines.examples: Permanent fabric marker, laundry marking pen, printed woven name tapes, iron-on name labels
skuLines.seasonality: Hard spike at every admission and term start (Apr, Jul); again after uniform issue
skuLines.notes: A residential school requires every uniform item to be named, and a few thousand children arrive each year with a trunk of unnamed clothes — so this is a near-certain, calendar-driven must-have that a generic laundry assortment would never contain. Almost weightless, excellent margin, and it pairs into a paid marking service at the clothing store. One of the clearest opportunities in this lane.

skuLines.line: Sewing kit, buttons, safety pins & hooks
skuLines.examples: Travel sewing kit, needle-and-thread card, assorted buttons, safety pins, saree pins, hook-and-eye, iron-on patches
skuLines.seasonality: Term time; peaks at term start and after sports season
skuLines.notes: A washed-and-worn uniform loses buttons weekly and there is no tailor 30km away at 9pm. Highest percentage margin in the lane, negligible freight, and it keeps a resident's trip from becoming a trip to town. Sits naturally between laundry and the clothing store.

skuLines.line: Naphthalene balls, camphor & silica damp/moth protection
skuLines.examples: Naphthalene balls, camphor tablets, silica gel sachets, neem-based moth repellent, cedar blocks
skuLines.seasonality: Jun-Sep monsoon (damp cupboards, mildew) and Mar-Apr when woollens go into storage
skuLines.notes: A cold, heavy-monsoon hill cupboard grows mildew on stored clothes, and woollens put away in March come out in October eaten or musty. Sits on the boundary with household pest control — shelve it here because the job is clothes, and cross-merchandise with the woollen liquid and garment covers. Note residents will ask for camphor for religious use too, so keep the two uses separated at the shelf.

skuLines.line: Garment covers & seasonal woollen storage bags
skuLines.examples: Non-woven suit/saree cover, zippered garment bag, vacuum compression storage bag, under-bed storage bag
skuLines.seasonality: Mar-Apr (woollens away) and Sep-Oct (woollens out, cottons away)
skuLines.notes: Two clean selling moments a year, driven by a real six-month winter. Vacuum bags earn their keep in a hostel or a small quarters where storage is the binding constraint. Light, flat-packed, easy freight — pair with the moth/damp line.

skuLines.line: White PT-shoe whitener, shoe shampoo & brush
skuLines.examples: White canvas shoe whitener liquid, shoe shampoo/cleaner, Cherry Blossom white, shoe cleaning brush
skuLines.seasonality: Term time; every PT/sports day and inspection; heaviest in monsoon mud
skuLines.notes: White canvas PT shoes are part of a school uniform and are inspected, so they are washed and whitened weekly by thousands of children. Formally a footwear-care line, but the buyer buys it in the same trip and for the same reason as blue whitener — shelve it with laundry. Genuine demand this population has and a normal store's laundry aisle does not serve.

skuLines.examples: Bundle: delicates or mild liquid detergent + Ujala Supreme + Revive starch + steel pegs + extra-long line
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks before Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Nagar Kirtan and function weeks
skuLines.notes: The one bundle this store can build that no national retailer would: washing, blueing, starching and stretching 5-6 metres of voile is a specific weekly job for most of a 5,000-person Sikh campus, and today it takes four separate purchases and some knowledge. Bundling it raises basket size, blends margin above the thin single-SKU rates, and makes the store the place that understands the customer. Same logic as a hostel starter kit at admission.

trends2026: Liquid detergent is the category's growth engine — still only ~10-15% of Indian laundry value but growing several times faster than powder, with 'matic' liquid now the default for every new washing machine. Semi-urban and small-town India is where the next leg comes from, which is exactly this store's profile.

Refill pouches and concentrates went mainstream in 2025-26, pushed by both EPR/plastic-waste rules and by consumers noticing the per-wash saving. For a store 30-50km up a hill road this is a freight and breakage story as much as an environmental one: a pouch ships at a fraction of a bottle's weight and cube and does not crack.

GST 2.0 (effective 22 Sep 2025) moved soaps and detergent/washing preparations into the 5% slab from 18%. Landed cost and MRP ladders across the whole lane reset — verify the exact HSN line before repricing or renegotiating with the distributor rather than trusting a remembered rate.

Hygiene-positioned laundry additives (Comfort Anti-Bacterial, Dettol/Savlon laundry sanitiser) have settled into a permanent sub-segment rather than fading as a COVID artefact — and in a heavy-monsoon climate where clothes dry indoors, they solve a real mildew-and-odour problem, not a perceived one.

Fabric conditioner penetration is climbing off a low base (roughly a tenth of Indian households) almost entirely on the back of ₹1-₹5 sachets, which is the format that reaches students and hostel buyers.

Laundry sheets, strips and pods are the new-format story of 2025-26, arriving via D2C and quick commerce. Near-weightless, so they are the most freight-advantaged item a remote hill store could test — with the caveat that pods are a poisoning hazard around the small children and babies on this campus.
Eco and plant-based brands (Beco, Koparo, The Better Home, Bhuumi) scaled through marketplaces and q-commerce, bringing 25-40% margins into a category otherwise stuck in single digits.

Quick commerce reshaped pack-size strategy nationally into a barbell — sachet or single-serve at one end, 4kg and refill at the other, with mid-sizes squeezed. A closed township has no q-commerce competitor, so the store can run that barbell deliberately for its own economics instead of defensively.

Washing-machine penetration keeps rising in semi-urban and staff-quarters India, dragging matic powder and low-foam liquid demand up with it, and creating a small but real market for portable/mini washers in single rooms and hostels.
adjacentServices: Wash-and-fold laundry service billed per kg — the single biggest attach available. A 5,000-person residential campus with cold water and a monsoon is the ideal captive base, and the store already sells the inputs at 8% margin; the service earns 40-60% on the same detergent.

Ironing and pressing counter priced per garment, with a dedicated dastaar/patka starch-and-press line. Starching and tying a turban is a weekly skilled job for most of this campus and is the highest-frequency service opportunity on site.

Seasonal woollen, blanket and quilt washing — a drop-off drive in March-April as winter bedding is put away and again in September-October as it comes out. Two predictable revenue events a year that no household can do itself in a hill quarters.

Dry-cleaning agency: collect on campus, aggregate weekly, run one van to Solan/Nahan/Chandigarh. The store takes a commission and the resident avoids a 60-100km round trip — this converts an off-campus wallet leak into store revenue.

Uniform name-marking and minor-repair service at the clothing store — printed name tapes stitched or ironed on, buttons, hems, zips. Sells at every admission, needs one machine and one person, and pairs directly with the name-tape and sewing SKU lines.

Bulk/institutional supply contract to the hostels, mess, canteens, F&V counter and guest house on a monthly indent: sacks, 5L bleach cans, institutional bleach and low-foam matic powder. Turns thin retail margin into contracted, forecastable volume and fixes the pre-monsoon stocking problem.

Liquid-detergent refill station (bring your own bottle, dispense by the litre). Cuts hill freight and plastic at once, prices below the bottle, and holds margin — the clearest structural fit between this category and this location.

Hostel starter laundry kit sold at admission: bucket, mug, bar, powder sachets, hangers, pegs, mesh bag, name marker, sewing kit. One SKU, high blended margin, sold to every arriving student on a known date.

Washing-machine servicing and hard-water descaling visits for staff quarters — iron-bearing hill water scales machines and irons, and there is no service centre nearby. Attaches to the washing soda, descaler and ironing-water lines.
Seasonal rental or deposit-back scheme on indoor drying racks for the monsoon term, so a resident who needs one for ten weeks does not have to buy and store a bulky stand.
